title: Conditional modulation with sparse private residual
hypothesis: A shared conditional low-rank view plus sparse private residuals retains function quality across growing task heterogeneity with fewer bytes than independent operators, and identifies where private state becomes necessary.
physical_object: shared 8x8 base operator and rank-2 shared task basis
mirror_coordinate: per-task basis coefficients plus sparse private residual entries
controls: Mirror plus sparse private residual fractions

development.selection_metric: nMSE-byte frontier and private fraction at threshold

fresh.reason: Direct coefficient basis is matched and the registered frontier is synthetic mechanism evidence.

success_gate: At heterogeneity <=0.3, residual fraction <0.25 reaches nMSE <=1e-3 and saves >=20% bytes over independent operators.
failure_gate: No residual fraction below 0.5 meets nMSE <=1e-3 at heterogeneity <=0.3, or shared/private bytes never beat independent storage.
boundaries: no trained PEFT or natural task claim
no fresh worlds if direct control aliases Mirror
Magnitude top-k oracle selection gives an optimistic residual frontier, not a learned residual allocator.
